title: The Ledger and the Network: from a Jezzine boy's crossing to the telephones of a continent
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Mountain Town and the Crossing

stops.name: Jezzine, a son under Ottoman rule
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim), which gives the birth date and the birth name Khalil Salim Haddad Aglamaz; the conscription motive and the brothers' 1898 departure come from the family's own documentary narrative and are reconstruction.
stops.campa: In a Maronite mountain town above the Sidon plain, in a Lebanon that is a province of the Ottoman Empire, a boy is registered as Khalil Salim Haddad Aglamaz. Families here count their sons against the year the Ottoman levy will come for them, and the sons tend to leave before it arrives. Four of his older brothers sail for the Americas in 1898, and for four more years he stays on in the town with his parents. He follows them in 1902, at fourteen years old, still carrying the name in the register.
suggested_refs: The Maronite emigration out of Ottoman Mount Lebanon, 1880s-1900s

stops.name: Port of Veracruz, fourteen and without Spanish
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the year comes from the family's documentary narrative, and the specific port of entry could not be independently confirmed. Day and month defaulted to order the segment.
stops.campa: The ship comes in at the Gulf port that handles most of what enters Mexico, and down the gangway walks a fourteen-year-old with no Spanish and nobody meeting him at the water. Ahead of him are brothers he has not seen in four years. Mexico in 1902 is eight years from a revolution nobody in the customs shed expects, and it is taking in Levantine arrivals faster than it can spell their names. Over the next decade the clerks write his name down a dozen ways before it settles as Julián Slim Haddad.
suggested_refs: Ottoman-passport records of Levantine arrivals at Veracruz, 1890s-1910s
sources: Colegio Invisible dossier, family-history section (port unconfirmed)

stops.name: Tampico, the brothers who went first
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from the family's documentary narrative; not independently confirmed. Month defaulted to place the arrival after the crossing.
stops.campa: Four hundred kilometers up the coast, in the river and oil town of Tampico, José, Elías, Carlos and Pedro have been trading four years already. The youngest joins them here. This is how the Levantine emigration works in Mexico: one brother crosses, sends for the next, and the family reassembles in a country none of them chose for any reason except that it would let them in. The commercial center of gravity will move to the capital soon enough. For now it is a shopfront on a hot street near the Pánuco.
suggested_refs: The Lebanese commercial colony of Tampico, Tamaulipas, at the turn of the century

stops.name: Centro Histórico, La Estrella de Oriente
stops.date_confidence: conflicted and unresolved: the family's English- and Spanish-language biographies give 1904 and 1911 for the founding, and neither could be independently confirmed. The May 1914 buyout of Jose's half for 30,000 pesos comes from the family archive and is reconstruction. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: The brothers open a dry-goods house in the old center of the capital and call it the Star of the East. Bolts of cloth, buttons, thread, the trade of merchants with capital in their hands and none of it in a bank. In May 1914 Julian buys out his brother José's half for thirty thousand pesos. The Revolution is running through the streets outside, and property in the center is priced at whatever a man who wants out will take. He goes on buying downtown lots through the war years.
suggested_refs: Deeds and downtown property purchases of Julián Slim Haddad, 1914-1920
sources: Colegio Invisible dossier, family-archive figures (founding date contradicted between the family's own two biographies)

stops.name: Hidalgo del Parral, born to a press that sets Arabic
stops.date_confidence: birthplace attested: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim states Linda Helú Atta was born in Parral, Chihuahua. Her birth year is not established in any source reviewed and the date here orders the segment only. The publishing detail follows en-wiki, which says her parents founded one of the first Arabic-language magazines in Mexico; the dossier's stronger claim that José Helú imported an early Arabic printing press is unconfirmed.
stops.campa: In a silver town in Chihuahua, a long way north of any Lebanese quarter, Linda Helú Atta is born to José Helú and Wadiha Atta. Her parents set type in Arabic: one of the first Arabic-language magazines printed in Mexico comes off their press, made for a community scattered thin across a country that cannot read it. She will marry Julián Slim Haddad and keep his accounts. Which of the six children she raises learn the ledger from her and which from him is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Surviving issues of the early Arabic-language press of the Mexican mahjar

segments.name: The Ledger and the First Bond

stops.name: Mexico City, the fifth of six
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim; Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú').
stops.campa: Carlos Slim Helú is born in the capital on the twenty-eighth of January, fifth of the six children of Julián Slim Haddad and Linda Helú Atta. The house is Lebanese-Mexican and mercantile: Maronite Catholic, Arabic at its edges, Spanish at its center, organized around a business in the old town that survived a revolution by buying during it. Nobody in the family is poor and nobody in it is idle. Mexico has just nationalized its oil and is about to spend forty years growing.
suggested_refs: The Slim Helu household in Mexico City, 1940s

stops.name: Mexico City, the allowance and the notebook
stops.date_confidence: attested for the sequence (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim): a government savings bond at eleven in 1951, a first stock purchase at twelve in an unnamed Mexican bank, and only by fifteen a shareholding in Mexico's largest bank. Britannica compresses the two purchases and attaches Banamex to the age-eleven bond; that attribution is not supported and is not used here. The household bookkeeping practice is tradition, corroborated in profiles but not from a primary document. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: Every child in the house is given an allowance and a ruled notebook, and every peso has to be written down: what came in, what went out, what is left. The father audits. At eleven Carlos puts his money into a government savings bond and watches the interest accumulate in his own handwriting. At twelve he buys shares outright in a Mexican bank. By fifteen he holds stock in the largest bank in the country, and he is still a schoolboy. He keeps the notebooks.
suggested_refs: The surviving childhood account books of the Slim Helu children

stops.name: Mexico City, the auditor dies
stops.date_confidence: attested that Julián Slim Haddad died when Carlos was thirteen (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'); the exact date is not established in any source reviewed and day and month are defaulted.
stops.campa: Julián Slim Haddad dies when his fifth son is thirteen. The man who crossed the Atlantic at fourteen without Spanish leaves behind downtown property, a dry-goods business, and six children who have all been taught to keep accounts. Nothing in the reviewed record fixes the day or even the month of the death, only the year and the son's age. The notebooks continue after him, same hand, same columns. The record does not preserve what the boy said, or whether he said anything at all.
suggested_refs: The estate of Julián Slim Haddad, Mexico City, 1953

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, the algebra class
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1961 professional degree (carlosslim.com/biografia_ing.html) and for the teaching (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim); es.wikipedia.org gives the UNAM years as 1958-1962, so the exit year is in conflict and both are recorded. Coordinates corrected to the Facultad de Ingeniería in Ciudad Universitaria; the dossier's 19.3299, -99.1852 falls about 350 m southwest in open ground. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He reads civil engineering at the national university and completes his professional studies in 1961, and while still a student he stands at the front of a room in the same faculty teaching algebra and linear programming. Linear programming is the mathematics of extracting the most from a constrained system: what to buy, at what price, under which limits. He never builds a bridge. His own biography dates the degree to 1961; the Spanish record gives his years at the faculty as 1958 to 1962.
suggested_refs: Course records of the Facultad de Ingeniería, UNAM, 1958-1962

stops.name: Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, the first firm
stops.date_confidence: attested for the founding year (carlosslim.com/biografia_ing.html: Founded Inversora Bursatil in 1965) and for Jarritos del Sur the same year (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim). Britannica's US$400,000 is misdescribed as one year's profit; it is the accumulated trading capital he held by 1965. Coordinates are the exchange's historic Calle Uruguay site in the Centro Histórico. His later vice-chairmanship of the exchange and chairmanship of the brokerage-firms association are reconstruction and carry no separate stop. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: Four years out of the university he has traded his way to roughly four hundred thousand dollars of his own capital, and he puts it into a brokerage house of his own, Inversora Bursatil, which will become the nucleus of Grupo Financiero Inbursa. The same year he buys a soft-drink bottler, Jarritos del Sur. One purchase gives him a seat on the exchange to raise money with; the other is a dull cash-generating business to raise it for. He is twenty-five years old.
suggested_refs: Founding papers of Inversora Bursatil, 1965

stops.name: Mexico City, Carso, cut from two names
stops.date_confidence: attested (carlosslim.com/biografia_ing.html): Inmobiliaria Carso established January 1966, the name combining Car from Carlos and so from Soumaya. The dossier's 'Inmuebles Carso' is the wrong company name. The marriage year is in conflict and is not resolved: carlosslim.com and es.wikipedia.org give 1966, en.wikipedia.org and Britannica give 1967. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: In January he sets up a real-estate company and names it by cutting two names in half: Car from Carlos, so from Soumaya. Soumaya Domit Gemayel is Lebanese-Mexican like him, connected to the Gemayel family of Lebanese politics, and by his own official biography he marries her the same year. English-language accounts place the wedding in 1967 instead, which would mean the company carried her name a year before she did. Nothing reviewed settles which is right.
suggested_refs: Incorporation record of Inmobiliaria Carso, January 1966

stops.name: New York Stock Exchange, the Latin American committee
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and the date is a segment-ordering device only. The role is attested by his own official biography (carlosslim.com/biografia_ing.html: he chaired the Latin American Committee of the New York Stock Exchange's Board), but no source located gives a year; the dossier's '1970s' is unsupported, and its 'first president' overstates a first-party source that says only 'chaired.' Coordinates verified against the exchange at 11 Wall Street.
stops.campa: A Mexican broker takes the chair of the exchange's Latin American committee at Eleven Wall Street. It is a small institutional office and it puts him inside the room where North American capital decides what a Latin American company is worth. His companies will list here in time. Every source that mentions the post omits the year. The biography he authorizes lists what he did and is sparing about when; the date of this chairmanship is not in it, and no other source supplies one.
suggested_refs: Board and committee minutes of the New York Stock Exchange concerning its Latin American Committee

stops.name: Mexico City, everything under one company
stops.date_confidence: attested that the holdings were consolidated under Grupo Galas, later renamed Grupo Carso (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'). The claim that he had established or acquired at least seven further businesses by 1972 is reconstruction. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: By the turn of the decade the holdings have multiplied past what a man can carry in a notebook: a brokerage, a bottler, property, printing, tobacco, construction materials. He gathers them under one company, Grupo Galas, which will later be renamed Grupo Carso. Mexico in 1980 is drunk on oil revenue and cheap dollar debt, and everyone with a balance sheet is borrowing against both. Grupo Galas is the name on the consolidated holding for the next ten years, and it enters the decade holding cash.
suggested_refs: Corporate history of Grupo Galas / Grupo Carso

segments.name: Buying in the Year Everyone Sells

stops.name: Mexico City, the crisis year
stops.date_confidence: attested that the 1982 contraction and debt crisis was the occasion of a wave of acquisitions of distressed but operating companies (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'). Day and month defaulted to the year.
stops.campa: The peso collapses, the banks are nationalized, foreign capital runs for the border, and every operating Mexican company is worth whatever a buyer holding cash will say it is. Slim holds cash. He buys: cigarettes, copper, chemicals, retail, insurance, anything that still turns a profit under a government that has run out of dollars. He is forty-two. Twelve years later he will write that fear is the worst of a man's feelings, that it weakens him and stops him acting.
stops.quote: Los miedos son los peores sentimientos del hombre, lo debilitan, lo inhiben a la acción y lo deprimen.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, carlosslim.com/carta.html (written twelve years later)
suggested_refs: Acquisition records of Grupo Galas during the 1982-1988 debt crisis

stops.name: Mexico City, an insurance company for thirteen million
stops.date_confidence: attested (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'): Seguros de México acquired for a reported US$13 million and later integrated into what became Grupo Financiero Inbursa. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He pays about thirteen million dollars for an insurance company. Insurance collects money now against claims that fall due later, which means the insurer holds and invests other people's money in the interval. Seguros de México becomes part of what grows into Grupo Financiero Inbursa, and Inbursa becomes the balance sheet standing behind everything else: the brokerage, the acquisitions, the bids that come later. The engineer who taught constrained optimization has bought a pool of money that is legally his to invest and not yet anybody's to claim. He is forty-four years old.
suggested_refs: Acquisition of Seguros de México, 1984, and the formation of Grupo Financiero Inbursa

stops.name: Casa de los Azulejos, the tiled house comes with the chain
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year Grupo Carso acquired Sanborns (es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanborns: 'En el año de 1985, la empresa fue adquirida por el Grupo Carso'). The dossier's 1997 is wrong; 1997 is the Sears Roebuck de México year. The Sanborn brothers bought the House of Tiles in 1917 and opened the branch in 1919, so the chain, not the building, is what changed hands. Coordinates from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_de_los_Azulejos. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: Grupo Carso acquires Sanborns, and with the chain comes its flagship: a colonial mansion on Madero faced entirely in blue and white Puebla tile, a national monument with a restaurant under its covered patio and a store behind it. The Sanborn brothers bought the house in 1917 and put a soda fountain in it two years later. The building is older than that by centuries, rebuilt in 1793 and tiled in 1737. What changes hands in 1985 is the chain, not the house.
suggested_refs: The Casa de los Azulejos, Avenida Francisco I. Madero 4, Mexico City

stops.name: Mexico City, the cigarette money
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier places the Cigatam acquisition in the 1980s without a year and gives no site finer than the capital; the date orders the segment only. The 2007 sale of the 50.1% stake to Philip Morris International for about US$1.1 billion is separately reported and also reconstruction (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú').
stops.campa: He takes the Mexican tobacco business tied to Philip Morris, and cigarettes turn out to be the engine. Smokers pay daily, in cash, in every corner shop in the country, and the money arrives faster than any acquisition can spend it. Through the debt-crisis years that stream funds the buying of everything else. Later, when his foundations begin paying for hospitals and health programs, the origin of the money is raised against him. In 2007 he sells the majority stake to Philip Morris International for about one point one billion dollars.
suggested_refs: Cigatam and the Philip Morris International transaction of 2007

stops.name: Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, Grupo Carso goes public
stops.date_confidence: attested that Grupo Carso listed in 1990 and that Porcelanite was acquired the same year (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'); the June date and the renaming of Grupo Galas at listing are reconstruction from corporate history. Nacobre and Química Fluor in 1988 are reconstruction (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'). Coordinates are the exchange's historic Centro Histórico site.
stops.campa: Grupo Carso lists its shares on the Mexican exchange and takes outside money for the first time, having been until now a private accumulation of one family's purchases. The tile maker Porcelanite is bought the same year; the copper manufacturer Nacobre and the chemical company Química Fluor came two years before. The group spans metals, chemicals, tobacco, retail, construction and paper. In December the government puts the national telephone company up for sale.
suggested_refs: Listing prospectus of Grupo Carso, Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, 1990

stops.name: Mexico City, the state telephone company is sold
stops.date_confidence: attested for the consortium and for the roughly US$1.76 billion paid for a controlling 20.4% block (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telefonos_de_Mexico, which also confirms the long controversy over the payment structure). No venue is documented: the dossier staged this at Los Pinos and conceded the presidential residence was an inference, the auction was run by the Secretaría de Hacienda, and no source places any part of it there, so the stop sits on the capital's general pin. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: A consortium of Grupo Carso, Southwestern Bell and France Câbles et Radio wins the sale of Teléfonos de México, paying roughly one and three quarter billion dollars for a controlling block of twenty and four tenths percent. The state hands over the whole national telephone network, monopoly intact, to a group with a Mexican holding company at its head. The financing terms, and what the government might have charged instead, will be argued over for three decades. No source records the room it was signed in.
suggested_refs: The 1990 privatization file of Teléfonos de México, Secretaría de Hacienda y Credito Publico

stops.name: Parque Vía 190, running the network
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Telmex's registered principal office is at Parque Vía 190 in the Cuauhtemoc borough (es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telmex); the dossier placed the headquarters on Insurgentes Sur beside the Cuicuilco reserve, which is a Telmex corporate campus but not the registered seat, and asserted the América Móvil spin-off was directed from there, which no source supports. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: From the corporate offices of Teléfonos de México the network is rebuilt: digital switching, tariffs restructured, obligations written into the concession and audited against it. The concession title fixes coverage targets and the dates by which they must be met. New lines go into towns that had been waiting years for one. Mexico gets telephones. Mexico also pays some of the highest connection prices in the developed world for them, and says so, loudly, for twenty-five years.
suggested_refs: The Telmex concession title and its investment obligations, 1990-2000

stops.name: Mexico City, the letter to the young
stops.date_confidence: attested: the letter is published on his own site as 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' dated June 1994 (carlosslim.com/carta.html). Day defaulted.
stops.campa: He writes a letter addressed to young people and puts it out under his own name. It is short, plain and unbusinesslike: on fear as the worst of the human feelings, on giving without expecting return, on the road of life being very long and traveled very fast. It becomes the most widely quoted thing he ever writes, reprinted on classroom walls and in motivational pamphlets he had nothing to do with. It is dated June 1994 and is still posted on his own website.
stops.quote: El éxito no es hacer bien o muy bien las cosas y tener el reconocimiento de los demás. Es la armonía del alma y de sus emociones, que necesita del amor, la familia, la amistad, la autenticidad, la integridad.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, carlosslim.com/carta.html
suggested_refs: 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, full text on carlosslim.com

stops.name: Mexico City, Sears Roebuck de México
stops.date_confidence: attested (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú') that he acquired control of Sears Roebuck de México in 1997 and integrated it with Sanborns, and that Grupo Carso was split into three companies in 1996. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He takes control of Sears Roebuck de México and folds it into the Sanborns retail operation, so an American department-store name in Mexico now answers to a Mexican holding company. The year before, Grupo Carso had been split into three separate companies, a reorganization that sorts industry from retail from telecommunications and makes each piece separately valuable and separately sellable. Sanborns is by now a hundred and more stores, each one a restaurant, a pharmacy counter and a bookshop under a single roof.
suggested_refs: The 1996 three-way reorganization of Grupo Carso

stops.name: Houston, the valve
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and the date is in conflict. The dossier places emergency heart surgery in Houston in October 1997 with a transfusion of roughly 130 units; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim records exactly one heart surgery and dates it 1999. The dossier's separate 1999 'further heart surgery' item is very likely this same event counted twice. The Washington Post's 2003 profile 'Living on the Edge of Death' returns HTTP 403 and could not be read, and the hospital is not named in any reachable source.
stops.campa: A valve in his heart ruptures and he is operated on in Houston. There is a hemorrhage; the transfusion is reported at something near a hundred and thirty units of blood; he comes very close to dying and does not. Some weeks afterward a Mexican news report announces that he has died, and the share prices of his companies drop before the correction catches up. The correction is printed. No source reached names the hospital, and the English encyclopedia record dates his one heart operation to 1999 instead of 1997.
suggested_refs: Washington Post, 'Living on the Edge of Death' (2003), inaccessible: HTTP 403
sources: Colegio Invisible dossier, chronology and afterlife sections (conflicting tags)

stops.name: Mexico City, Soumaya
stops.date_confidence: attested that Soumaya Domit Gemayel died in 1999 at fifty of chronic kidney disease (Wikipedia, 'Museo Soumaya'; dossier synthesis drawing on Osorno); the exact date was not verified against a primary obituary and day and month are defaulted.
stops.campa: Soumaya Domit Gemayel dies at fifty of chronic kidney disease, waiting on a second transplant, after a marriage of more than three decades. He does not remarry. Her name has been inside his companies since 1966, cut in half and welded to his own, and it will go next onto a museum, a foundation, and a plaza in a district that does not exist yet. Almost everything publicly known about her is what carries her name afterward. She was fifty. He was fifty-nine.
stops.quote: El camino de la vida es muy largo, pero se transita muy rápido.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, carlosslim.com/carta.html
suggested_refs: The Fundacion Carlos Slim and the naming of the Museo Soumaya

stops.name: Mexico City, América Móvil is cut loose
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'América Móvil'): incorporated 25 September 2000 as Telmex spun its wireless and international mobile business off from landline and internet operations.
stops.campa: Teléfonos de México cuts its wireless and international mobile business loose as a separate company, América Móvil, incorporated on the twenty-fifth of September. The landlines stay behind; the future walks out the door. What the new company sells is prepaid airtime, cards bought for small amounts in corner shops by people no credit bureau has ever assessed, across Latin America. Handsets go cheap because the handset is not the product. He explains the model by naming a razor company.
stops.quote: I call it the 'Gillette Plan' because in Gillette, you sell the razor...to sell shaves.
stops.quote_source: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/
suggested_refs: Incorporation documents of América Móvil, S.A.B. de C.V., 25 September 2000
sources: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/

stops.name: Centro Histórico, restoring the streets his father bought into
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim: chair of the restoration council since 2001), convened after a Vicente Fox advisory council. The criticism over property concentration and displacement pressure is dossier synthesis of press and academic coverage. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: After a presidential advisory council convenes, he chairs the executive committee for the rehabilitation of the historic center: a nonprofit foundation, tax incentives, police on the street, and a for-profit property vehicle buying buildings. Facades come back, restaurants open, the streets fill again in the evening. His father was buying property in these same blocks in 1914. Critics count how much of the restored downtown one family now owns and ask who had to leave for the rest to arrive.
stops.quote: Fighting poverty is now an economic need. It is not only a social issue
stops.quote_source: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/
suggested_refs: The Fideicomiso del Centro Histórico de la Ciudad de Mexico, from 2001
sources: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/

stops.name: Mexico City, the Chapultepec Agreement
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the accord and his role in promoting it are reported in reviewed corporate and foundation materials cross-checked against Britannica's career chronology, but no signing venue could be located, so the pin is city-level. The figure of more than 1.2 million endorsements is his own organization's count. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He promotes a national accord on investment, employment, rule of law and social development, signed by business, labor, academic and political figures who agree on very little else. His organization reports more than one point two million endorsements, a figure it counts itself and that nobody outside it audits. The document commits nobody to anything enforceable, and no mechanism is written into it for checking whether anyone tries. No source reached records the room where it was signed, the day, or the month; only the year is fixed.
stops.quote: Bad governments worry about the rich. Good governments worry about the poor.
stops.quote_source: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/
suggested_refs: The Acuerdo Nacional para la Unidad, el Estado de Derecho, el Desarrollo, la Inversion y el Empleo, 2005
sources: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/

stops.name: Mexico City, past Buffett
stops.date_confidence: attested (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú', dated figures): fortune estimated at US$53.1 billion, briefly second richest in the world; later the same year some private calculations ranked him first, ahead of Bill Gates.
stops.campa: His fortune is put at fifty-three point one billion dollars and he passes Warren Buffett into second place in the world. Later in the same year some private calculations place him first, ahead of Bill Gates. The money is not in software and not in American insurance. It is in Mexican telephone bills, paid monthly, in small amounts, by tens of millions of people, and in prepaid cards bought a hundred pesos at a time across a continent. That arithmetic had been visible for years.
suggested_refs: Forbes and private wealth estimates for 2007

stops.name: New York Times Building, two hundred and fifty million at fourteen percent
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'The New York Times Company'): a US$250 million loan at 14% interest with warrants attached, 20 January 2009. The initial 6.4% stake in 2008 is reconstruction (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú').
stops.campa: The New York Times Company is running out of cash in the worst winter American finance has had in seventy years. He lends it two hundred and fifty million dollars at fourteen percent, with warrants attached that can later be turned into stock. The paper takes it. Fourteen percent is not a rescue; it is a price, set by the only lender in the room. He had bought six point four percent of the company the year before. The warrants, if he exercises them, would make him its largest single shareholder.
stops.quote: No, the powerful ones are the media and the government.
stops.quote_source: Diego Enrique Osorno, 'Leer a Carlos Slim,' Gatopardo (2015), English at literalmagazine.com, answering whether he is the most powerful man in Mexico
suggested_refs: The January 2009 loan agreement and warrant terms, The New York Times Company
sources: Diego Enrique Osorno, 'Leer a Carlos Slim,' Gatopardo (2015), English at literalmagazine.com

stops.name: Mexico City, first on the list
stops.date_confidence: attested (Britannica, 'Carlos Slim Helú', Forbes ranking figure for 2010, cross-checked with the Forbes profile): ranked the world's richest person, a position held on the annual list through 2013.
stops.campa: Forbes puts him at the top of its list of the richest people in the world, a position he holds on the annual ranking through 2013. For four years the wealthiest man alive is a Mexican engineer who does his sums by hand and whose money comes out of a formerly state-owned telephone monopoly. American coverage treats this as an anomaly requiring explanation. In Mexico it explains itself, since everyone who has ever paid a phone bill knows where it came from.
stops.quote: When you need others to say good things about you, you will have a problem
stops.quote_source: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/
suggested_refs: Forbes annual billionaires lists, 2010-2013
sources: Academy of Achievement interview transcript, achievement.org/achiever/carlos-slim/

stops.name: Museo Soumaya, sixteen thousand hexagons
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museo_Soumaya): inaugurated 28 February 2011 and opened to the public 28 March 2011. The family's own page carlosslim.com gives 29 March; the Wikipedia date is followed here and the variant recorded. Coordinates from Wikipedia's own reading, about 135 m south of the dossier's afterlife-lens pin.
stops.campa: The museum opens to the public on the twenty-eighth of March, free, and it will stay free. Fernando Romero, his son-in-law, designed the building and engineered it with Ove Arup: a curved silver hyperboloid with no straight edge on it, skinned in sixteen thousand hexagonal aluminum tiles, standing in a district being built from nothing around it. The building carries his wife's name. Inside are more than sixty-six thousand objects across thirty centuries.
stops.quote: Al final nos vamos sin nada, sólo dejamos nuestras obras, familia, amigos y, quizá, una positiva influencia.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, carlosslim.com/carta.html
suggested_refs: The Museo Soumaya building at Plaza Carso, Fernando Romero with Ove Arup, 2011

stops.name: Basílica de Guadalupe, Plaza Mariana
stops.date_confidence: attested that the Plaza Mariana complex was inaugurated in 2011 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim); the month is not established and is defaulted to order the year. The Maronite Catholic family background is attested; nothing here is claimed about motive.
stops.campa: A plaza is inaugurated at the foot of the hill of Tepeyac, beside the basilica that receives more pilgrims than any other Catholic site in the Americas, and his philanthropy has paid for part of it. The Slim family is Maronite Catholic, an Eastern rite carried across the Atlantic by a fourteen-year-old with no Spanish. What the money builds is a forecourt: open paved ground for the crowds that arrive on the twelfth of December, when the basilica itself cannot hold them.
stops.quote: Cuando den, no esperen recibir. "Queda aroma en la mano que da rosas", dice un proverbio chino.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, 'Carta a los Jóvenes,' June 1994, carlosslim.com/carta.html
suggested_refs: The Plaza Mariana complex at the Basilica of Guadalupe, inaugurated 2011

stops.name: Plaza Carso, one address for all of it
stops.date_confidence: attested that most of the ventures share this headquarters complex in Colonia Granada beside the Plaza Antara mall (es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim, common headquarters address). The reading of the ownership structure as trusts and cross-shareholdings is dossier synthesis of the cited material. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: The companies converge on one complex in Colonia Granada, beside the Plaza Antara mall: offices, apartments, the museum, a theater, towers rising on land that was industrial a decade ago. The district acquires a name, Nuevo Polanco, and a reputation. Underneath the single address the ownership runs through trusts and cross-shareholdings layered until the sentence Slim owns that is a question for lawyers rather than a statement of fact. The address on the filings is the same for most of them.
suggested_refs: Plaza Carso and the Nuevo Polanco development, Colonia Granada, Mexico City

stops.name: New York Times Building, the warrants exercised
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'The New York Times Company'): 15.9 million Class A shares taken on exercise of the 2009 warrants, about 17.4% of Class A by March 2016, the stake halved to about 8% in December 2017 and gone from the above-5% holder list by 2021. The dossier misdates the earlier rise to 8.1% of Class A to 2012; it belongs to 2011. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He exercises the warrants from the 2009 loan, taking fifteen point nine million Class A shares, and becomes the largest shareholder in The New York Times Company, about seventeen percent of the Class A stock by March 2016. The Ochs-Sulzberger family holds the Class B shares and therefore the board, so the largest shareholder controls nothing at all. In December 2017 he sells half the position. By 2021 he is no longer listed among the holders above five percent.
suggested_refs: Class A and Class B share structure of The New York Times Company

stops.name: Lomas de Chapultepec, ninety square meters of shelving
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The library is described by Diego Enrique Osorno in 'Leer a Carlos Slim' (Gatopardo, 2015; English at literalmagazine.com), which places it in his office at Corporativo Financiero Inbursa; that building's coordinates were not verified, so the pin sits on Lomas de Chapultepec, the neighborhood he has long been associated with. The dossier misidentifies the Bush memoir as George W. Bush; the article says the memoirs of George Bush, senior. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: A reporter is walked along ninety square meters of shelving in his office at Corporativo Financiero Inbursa. The shelves hold biographies of industrialists, Bernard Baruch, J. Paul Getty, John D. Rockefeller Sr., books about businesses that failed, sports statistics, Mexican history. He pulls down the memoirs of George H. W. Bush and wants to talk about what Bush and Gorbachev agreed on. Asked whether he will give the collection to a university, he says no.
stops.quote: I almost never read theory. I don't like it.
stops.quote_source: Diego Enrique Osorno, 'Leer a Carlos Slim,' Gatopardo (2015), English at literalmagazine.com
suggested_refs: The private library at Corporativo Financiero Inbursa, described in Osorno's 2015 chronicle

stops.name: Rotterdam, the bid that is blocked
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPN; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America_Movil): a stake approaching 30% and an August 2013 offer of about 7.2 billion euros for the remaining 70%, stopped by a protective foundation's call option, with Dutch government opposition on national-security grounds. Coordinates corrected to KPN's Wilhelminakade 123 seat; the dossier's pin lay about 350 m north across the Maas basin. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: América Móvil has built a holding approaching thirty percent of the Dutch incumbent and now offers about seven point two billion euros for the rest. A stichting, a protective foundation of the kind Dutch company law keeps in reserve for exactly this, exercises a call option and the takeover stops. The government objects on national-security grounds as well. Through 2014 the position is unwound rather than converted, sold back down instead of turned into control.
suggested_refs: The KPN protective foundation and its 2013 call option

stops.name: Insurgentes Sur 1143, named the preponderant agent
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier reports the March 2014 designation of the América Móvil, Telmex, Telcel and Slim-family group as preponderant economic agent, and a 2021 Supreme Court ruling upholding it; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Federal_de_Telecomunicaciones mentions neither. Coordinates corrected to the IFT's stated address at Insurgentes Sur 1143, Col. Nochebuena; the dossier's pin sat about a kilometer north. The IFT itself was shuttered on 17 October 2025 and replaced by the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: The new telecommunications regulator measures the sector, finds one economic group holding more than half of it, and gives that finding a name in law: preponderant economic agent. América Móvil, Telmex, Telcel and the family are designated together. Asymmetric obligations follow, interconnection charges cut to zero, infrastructure opened to competitors, tariffs supervised. He complies with the measures and litigates against them at the same time, for years. In 2021 the Supreme Court upholds the designation; in October 2025 the regulator itself is shut down and replaced.
suggested_refs: The IFT preponderance resolution of March 2014 and its asymmetric measures

stops.name: Vienna, control of Telekom Austria
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telekom_Austria): on 23 April 2014 América Móvil took control by syndicate agreement with ÖIAG, spending as much as US$2 billion buying out minority shareholders and committing up to 1 billion euros of investment; the current split is América Móvil 58%, ÖBAG 28.42%. The dossier's '2012 onward' describes only when the stake was built. Coordinates corrected to the Lassallestrasse seat.
stops.campa: What the Dutch foundation refused, the Austrian state holding company signs. A syndicate agreement with ÖIAG hands América Móvil operating control of the former national telephone monopoly of Austria; as much as two billion dollars goes to buying out minority holders and up to a billion euros is committed in investment. A company created by the privatization of a Mexican state monopoly in 1990 is now the controlling shareholder of a privatized European one.
suggested_refs: The ÖIAG and América Móvil syndicate agreement, 23 April 2014

stops.name: Barcelona, recapitalizing FCC
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fomento_de_Construcciones_y_Contratas) for the Barcelona seat, the 2014 share issue, control by 2016, and the 2019 corporate corruption charge over alleged Panama-linked bribery predating his control. The exact date of the share issue was not verified and the month orders the year.
stops.campa: The Spanish construction group Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas is drowning in debt after the property crash, and he takes about a quarter of it in a rescue share issue, then control by 2016. Mexican money recapitalizes a company that spent a century building Spain: roads, water systems, waste collection. In 2019 Spanish prosecutors charge FCC as a corporate entity over alleged bribery routed through Panama, conduct predating his arrival. The charge is against the company, not the man.
suggested_refs: The 2014 FCC capital increase and the 2019 Panama corruption charge

stops.name: Texcoco, defending the airport
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the dossier reports his public defence of the Texcoco airport against candidate Andrés Manuel López Obrador and the cancellation after a disputed public consultation. Coordinates are approximate for the cancelled project site. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: On the drained bed of Lake Texcoco, east of the capital, a new international airport stands a third built. He defends it in public against a presidential candidate who has promised to cancel it, which is a rare thing for him: an open argument with the man about to win. Family businesses have exposure to the project. López Obrador wins, holds a consultation whose method is disputed from every side, and cancels the airport. Work stops, and what is already built stays standing on the lakebed.
suggested_refs: The cancelled Nuevo Aeropuerto Internacional de Mexico at Texcoco

stops.name: Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición, eighty years old with COVID
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the hospitalization (dossier); the institute's coordinates were confirmed by a separate geography fetch. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: He is eighty years old and admitted to the national institute of medical sciences and nutrition in Tlalpan, in the south of the capital, with COVID-19. Mexico in January 2021 is in the worst month of its epidemic and is burying people faster than it can count them. His health organizations are meanwhile working on vaccine supply for the region, which is a separate matter running on a separate clock. He is treated and sent home in good condition. The record fixes the month and not the day.
suggested_refs: The Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubiran, Tlalpan

stops.name: Tláhuac, the overpass between Olivos and Tezonco
stops.date_confidence: attested that an elevated section of Metro Line 12 collapsed on 3 May 2021 killing 26 people and that independent investigators identified construction deficiencies including defective studs and weld problems. Primary Reuters and AP coverage could not be fetched in this session and the Wikipedia article on the collapse returned 404, so the station pair and the DNV findings are carried as strongly corroborated secondary account. Carso's reconstruction of the section and its confidential compensation agreements without admission of liability are reconstruction.
stops.campa: On the night of the third of May a train crosses the elevated section between Olivos and Tezonco and the deck gives way beneath it. Twenty-six people are killed. The line was built by a consortium that included Grupo Carso's construction arm, CICSA. Independent investigators find construction defects: studs missing, studs badly welded, a deck that was never going to carry what it was built to carry. Carso rebuilds the section and reaches compensation agreements, kept confidential, admitting no legal liability.
suggested_refs: The independent DNV investigation into the Line 12 collapse, 2021
sources: Colegio Invisible dossier, geography section (primary coverage unfetchable this session)

stops.name: Zama field, Block 7, offshore Tabasco
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the transaction: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talos_Energy confirms the Zama discovery in Block 7 but says nothing about a 2023 Carso Zamajal purchase of 49.9% of Talos México, so the deal is downgraded from the dossier's attested tag. Coordinates corrected to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zama_oil_field; the dossier's 21.36, -92.4 lay roughly 270 km out of position, and the field is in the Sureste Basin offshore Tabasco rather than the Campeche Sound. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: Sixty kilometers off the coast of Tabasco, in shallow water over Block 7 of the Sureste Basin, lies one of the largest oil discoveries made in Mexican waters in decades. A Carso vehicle buys just under half of Talos México and the family group takes an indirect interest in the field. Pemex, the state company, remains the operator, because in Mexico the hydrocarbons underneath belong to the nation by constitutional article and the operator is the state. The telephone group is in oil.
suggested_refs: The Zama discovery, Block 7, Sureste Basin, and the Pemex operatorship

stops.name: One Braham, Aldgate: a position in BT
stops.date_confidence: attested for the June 2024 stake at 3.2%, raised to 4.3% by September 2024 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Group; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Slim); the roughly 400 million pound figure was not verified. Coordinates corrected to One Braham in Aldgate, BT's seat since November 2021; the dossier's pin matched neither One Braham nor the former BT Centre on Newgate Street. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: A family investment vehicle buys three point two percent of the British incumbent in June and raises it to four point three by September. No bid follows, no board seat is asked for, no operating role is taken: it is a position, held. The company it is a position in moved three years ago out of the headquarters it had occupied on Newgate Street into an eighteen-storey block in Aldgate. Whether anything further is intended, the disclosures do not say.

stops.name: Mexico City, the annual press conference
stops.date_confidence: attested for the conference and its published lines (carlosslim.com/desde-slim-conferencia-anual-26-mayo-2026_ing.html). The dossier's separate May 2026 report, flanked by Marco Antonio Slim Domit and Arturo Elías Ayub, announcing about US$5 billion of 2026 investment, endorsing elements of Plan México, criticizing Pemex production and ruling out fracking, is reconstruction. No venue is documented.
stops.campa: Eighty-six years old, flanked by his son Marco Antonio Slim Domit and his son-in-law Arturo Elías Ayub, he gives the press conference he gives every year. Five billion dollars of investment promised for the year. Parts of the president's plan endorsed, Pemex production criticized, fracking ruled out flatly. Then the arithmetic, which is the part he enjoys: from 1933 to 1981, forty-nine years, Mexico grew at six point two percent a year. The figure is in the transcript his office publishes the same day.
stops.quote: Mexico is experiencing favorable conditions to accelerate its economic growth
stops.quote_source: Carlos Slim, annual press conference, 26 May 2026, carlosslim.com/desde-slim-conferencia-anual-26-mayo-2026_ing.html
